name: Marvell Technology, Inc.
subtitle: 2027 Investment View
judgementTag: Hold existing positions and accumulate only on pullbacks
judgementText: Hold existing positions and accumulate only on pullbacks. This is a high- quality growth story, but the price already asks a lot of the earnings ramp. I would classify it as:

executiveSummary.label: Business outlook
executiveSummary.text: Strong and improving. Revenue grew 42.1% in the fiscal year ended Jan-2026 and accelerated sequentially for four straight quarters. Gross margin expanded and the company moved from losses to GAAP profit.

executiveSummary.label: Stock valuation
executiveSummary.text: Full to demanding. The trailing P/E is 75.2x, EV/Revenue is 21.3x, and the forward P/E is 31.2x. The forward figure depends on earnings far above current GAAP run-rate. In my scenarios the base case is roughly flat versus today's price.

executiveSummary.label: Risk-adjusted view
executiveSummary.text: Neutral to moderately positive for risk-tolerant investors, with a wide range of outcomes. Beta is 2.26, one-year annualised volatility is 80%, and the one-year maximum drawdown is -48.3%. Upside to the analyst mean target is large, but it is not reliable enough to bank on.

summaryNote: This is not a low-risk stock. A conservative investor should treat it as a small satellite position at most, or wait for a much lower entry price or clearer earnings delivery. All figures are in US dollars. Fiscal years end in January, so "FY2026" means the year ended 31- Jan-2026. The projection is for the share price at end-calendar-2027. Everything labelled "reported" comes from the supplied data. Everything labelled "assumption", "scenario" or "judgement" is mine.

sections.title: 1. Business Quality and Sector Positioning
sections.content:
Reported facts
- Marvell is a Technology / Semiconductors company with 7,480 employees. Its summary describes
data infrastructure semiconductors spanning the data-center core to the network edge.
- Products include ethernet and interconnect silicon (PAM, coherent and coherent-lite DSPs, silicon
photonics, co-packaged optics, linear pluggable optics, active electrical cable DSPs, PCIe retimers).
They also include custom ASICs, fibre channel, storage controllers, CXL/PCIe/NVMe, and UALink
and scale-up ethernet switching.
- It serves data centers, communications and other markets, sold through direct customers and
distributors.
- Sector context: XLK returned +25.5% over one year versus +13.4% for SPY, and sector
momentum is labelled positive. MRVL returned +172.1% over the same year, so it has far outrun its
sector.

- Goodwill. Goodwill is 49.6% of total assets (flag: above 30%). The company booked a 528.8M
asset impairment charge in FY2025, so write-down risk is not theoretical.
- Earnings-versus-cash divergence. The source flags net income exceeding operating cash flow
by 1,611.8M. The divergence is largely the roughly 1,830.4M non-cash gain on a business sale.
Excluding it, operating cash flow of 1,750.5M is about 2.1x underlying net income of roughly
839.7M (my calc). Free cash flow has been positive in all four years shown (no negative years).
- Capital allocation. FY2026 buybacks were 2,040.1M, dividends 205.1M and debt repayment
790.6M, against new debt issuance of 1,198.6M. Buybacks exceeded free cash flow of 1,391.9M
and were funded by divestiture proceeds of 2,478.6M, which are not repeatable.
- Share count. The balance sheet showed 847.3M shares at Jan-26. Current shares outstanding are
876.9M (+3.5%), and diluted average shares were 921.2M in the Jul-26 quarter. The cause is
unavailable. Check for new issuance or acquisition-related shares.
Judgement: Liquidity and leverage look comfortable. Cash of 2.6B covers the 499.8M of debt due
within a year. The weak spots are working-capital absorption and the goodwill-heavy asset base.
Reported net debt of 1,831.8M excludes leases of 319.7M, which is why it differs from total debt
minus cash (2,151.5M).

sections.title: 4. Order Book and Revenue Visibility
sections.content:
Reported order book, backlog, design-win pipeline, customer concentration and company
guidance are all unavailable in the supplied data. I will not estimate them.
What the data does offer as indirect visibility evidence:
- Revenue has risen sequentially for four consecutive quarters (+3.4%, +7.0%, +9.0%, +13.3%),
which shows a clear acceleration.
- Work-in-process inventory is up 56% and payables are up 72% (accounts payable 1,073.8M
versus 622.2M). This is consistent with the company preparing for higher volumes (inference, not
confirmation).
- Deferred revenue is only 40.1M, so there is no visible prepayment cushion.
- Receivables are up sharply, so some recent revenue has not yet turned into cash.
What to monitor: reported backlog or remaining performance obligations, management guidance
for the next quarter, customer concentration in the annual filing, any design-win announcements,
and whether quarter-on-quarter growth stays above about 8%.

- Bull: Revenue keeps compounding at 40% with strong operating leverage, and the market holds a

only works if the market keeps valuing adjusted or revenue-based metrics.

sections.title: 8. Growth Potential
sections.content:
Yes, in my judgement. The reasons, all from the data:
- Revenue growth accelerated to 13.3% quarter-on-quarter in the latest quarter, and year-on-year
growth was 36.5%.
- Gross margin has risen from 41.3% to 51.0% annually and to 53.1% in the latest quarter, which is
a sign of pricing power or favourable mix.
- Free cash flow has been positive in each of the four years shown. Return on equity (16.5%) is

reasonable on a goodwill-heavy book.
- Net debt fell and tangible book value turned positive (1,195.2M).
- The company is spending on R&D (25.3% of revenue, up 43% over five quarters), which supports
the product roadmap.
Limits on that potential
- Operating margin has stopped expanding (18.7% in Jan-26 versus 16.7% in Jul-26) as operating
expenses rose.
- Working-capital intensity is rising.
- The order book is unverified.
- The growth outlook is already in the price.
Conclusion: the business can plausibly keep growing. Whether the stock can deliver a return on
top of what is already priced in is the open question.

sections.title: 10. Bullish Triggers
sections.content:
Quarterly revenue growth staying at or above about 8% sequentially, with disclosed backlog or
guidance that supports it.
Operating margin returning above the 18.7% reached in Jan-26 and moving toward the 21% in
my base case.
Receivables growth falling back in line with revenue (DSO moving back toward about 65 days)
and inventory turnover recovering.
Clear evidence that the forward EPS of about $7.33 is reached, plus reconciliation of GAAP and
adjusted earnings.
A pullback toward $190–$210 (the base-case low end and the area between the lower Bollinger
band and the 200-day average), where the risk/reward improves.
Price recovering above the 50-day average ($242.91) and then the 20-day resistance ($286.95)
on rising volume.

sections.title: 11. Bearish Triggers
sections.content:
A sequential revenue slowdown below about 5%, or a cut in guidance.
Gross margin falling back below about 51%, or operating margin below about 14.5%.
Receivables or inventory continuing to build faster than revenue.
Another impairment, or evidence that the roughly 1.83B gain was masking weak underlying
earnings.
Continued share-count growth without matching earnings growth.
A daily close below $223.47 support on heavy volume, then below the $217.88 lower Bollinger
band.
Further reduction by large active holders (as with Fidelity at -56.6%).

sections.content:
Hold existing positions; accumulate only on pullbacks. Do not chase.

A tactical long is defensible near the lower band with a
defined stop (below $217.88) and a smaller position,
given the oversold RSI and the OBV divergence. Accept
that the base case offers little upside and the bear case
is severe.
Conservative investors
Avoid, or hold only a small satellite position. An 80%
volatility and a possible 48%-type drawdown do not
suit capital-preservation goals.
Best overall judgement: Marvell looks like a high-quality, fast-growing business with real operating
improvement and positive cash flow. The stock, however, is priced for strong execution. My
scenarios give a roughly flat base case, a probability-weighted value near $224, and a wide spread
from about $102 to $341. The business deserves a place on the watchlist and a small position for
risk-tolerant investors. A better entry or clearer evidence on backlog, margins, receivables and
adjusted earnings would improve the risk/reward.

outcomes. Beta is 2.26, one-year annualised volatility is 80%, and the one-year maximum

8. Does the company still have potential to grow?
Yes, in my judgement. The reasons, all from the data:
- Revenue growth accelerated to 13.3% quarter-on-quarter in the latest quarter, and year-on-year
growth was 36.5%.
- Gross margin has risen from 41.3% to 51.0% annually and to 53.1% in the latest quarter, which is
a sign of pricing power or favourable mix.
- Free cash flow has been positive in each of the four years shown. Return on equity (16.5%) is

reasonable on a goodwill-heavy book.
- Net debt fell and tangible book value turned positive (1,195.2M).
- The company is spending on R&D (25.3% of revenue, up 43% over five quarters), which supports
the product roadmap.
Limits on that potential
- Operating margin has stopped expanding (18.7% in Jan-26 versus 16.7% in Jul-26) as operating
expenses rose.
- Working-capital intensity is rising.
- The order book is unverified.
- The growth outlook is already in the price.
Conclusion: the business can plausibly keep growing. Whether the stock can deliver a return on
top of what is already priced in is the open question.
